verses.text: The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing.
They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.
In their streets, they clothe themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.
Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.
My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for on the way to Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.
For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.
Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.
For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.

footnotes.content: A 'burden' in Isaiah's mouth is a heavy word—not just bad news, but a sorrow that prophets carry on behalf of the Lord. Ar and Kir, cities of Moab, fall in one night: sudden, complete. I've learned that judgment never surprises the Lord, though it should break our hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baldness and shaved beards were signs of deepest grief in that world—sacred sorrow. The nobles climb to the high places not to pray for rescue, but to weep where the Lord can see them grieve. Even in judgment, there is something true in tears that finally face reality.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sackcloth in the streets. When a whole city puts on ashes and cloth, it is a public confession: 'We are laid bare, we are nothing.' This is the beginning of repentance—though too late to avert the judgment, sorrow spoken aloud is never wasted in the Lord's sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out to each other—fear travels city to city. The armed men cry aloud, but their arms cannot save them. 'Their souls tremble within them' is the sound of a people who finally know: strength is not in soldiers. Only Jesus can give the trembling soul true peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaiah's own heart cries out—he is not distant from Moab's suffering. He names the flight to Zoar and Eglath Shelishiyah as women, nobles, children scatter like frightened animals. The prophet grieves a people he could not turn. Love that goes unheeded is the deepest kind of loneliness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The waters of Nimrim lie desolate—even nature's life seems to drain away. Not a drop of green remains. This is not poetic exaggeration to an ancient reader; it is the picture of what happens when a land is abandoned by the Lord's hand. Yet see how the Lord always leaves a remnant for those who turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their wealth—hard-gotten, carefully stored—they must leave behind, fording the brook with only what they carry. Possessions become baggage. I've seen in long years how swiftly the things we cling to slip through our fingers. The Lord teaches this lesson to every generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cry echoes from border to border—Eglaim to Beer Elim. The whole nation is one wound, one voice of anguish. When judgment comes, it reaches everywhere, spares no corner. Yet even in the sound of sorrow, a heart can still cry out to the Lord and be heard.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dimon's waters full of blood, and more judgment yet to come. Readers today hear an echo in this: calamity piled on calamity, judgment that does not relent. But we who have seen the Cross know that Jesus bore our judgment so that we would not face Moab's fate. His blood, shed once, ends the need for any more.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
